content.text:
Interesting: Initiation notice says hearings April 28-May 1; June proposal says hearings April 28-29 and nearly 60 witnesses. That could be a factual update, not discrepancy. Q14 statement 2 says "USTR received over 450 written comments on the proposed action and heard nearly 60 witnesses." The 450/nearly 60 figures are in the June proposal describing response to the *initiation notice*, not the proposed action. So incorrect.

Now, Q11 might not require section 301 discrepancies beyond maybe one. But the prompt says "documents of the section 301 forced-labor action and of the section 338 actions"—could list section 338 discrepancies only, but then why mention section 301? There must be at least one. Let's find a clear one.

Compare June proposal's Annex A note: "In addition to the products listed in this Annex, the proposed action does not cover informational materials, donations, accompanied baggage; all articles and parts of articles that are subject to section 232 tariffs; USMCA-compliant goods of Canada or Mexico; and textiles..." The final notice at 47318 summarizes the proposal's exemptions as "informational materials, donations, accompanied baggage, all articles and parts of articles subject to tariffs under Section 232, and certain products identified in Annex A." It omits USMCA Canada/Mexico and CAFTA textiles. Not a contradiction, just incomplete. But Q11 says "a statement ... about what another document ... says or does, differs." Incompleteness isn't necessarily difference.

What about final notice at 47318: "The June 5, 2026 FRN proposed applying tariffs of 10 percent for each economy that imposes a forced labor import prohibition; has taken on commitments ...; or has imposed a partial regime..." The June proposal's actual 10% list includes Ecuador and Indonesia twice, and only specific economies. "Each economy that imposes a forced labor import prohibition" is overbroad because many investigated economies impose some form of forced labor import prohibition but are not in the 10% list? The June proposal's determinations say 54 economies failed to impose and effectively enforce; six failed to effectively enforce (meaning they impose). So only six impose. The phrase "each economy that imposes" = those six; okay.

What about final notice line 165: "The June 5, 2026 FRN proposed applying tariffs of 10 percent for each economy that imposes a forced labor import prohibition..."—it does not mention that the proposal also included a textile mechanism at a *reduced* (not zero) rate, while the memo says "zero section 301 tariff rate" (line 152). Aha! The June proposal (line 331-333) says "a textile mechanism that would allow for a certain volume of apparel and textile imports to enter the United States at a reduced Section 301 tariff rate." The memo recital (line 150-152) says "the Trade Representative proposed to establish a textile mechanism that would allow a certain volume of apparel and textile imports to enter the United States at a zero section 301 tariff rate." That's a discrepancy! The memo describes the proposal as zero; the proposal says reduced. The final notice at 47318 says "proposed a textile mechanism that would allow ... at a reduced Section 301 tariff rate" (line 158-161). So the memo's "zero" differs from June proposal's "reduced." This is a clear discrepancy. Cite memo 91 FR 47719 vs June proposal 91 FR 34274. Great.

Any other section 301 discrepancy:
- Memo recital line 134-144 says "The Trade Representative proposed tariffs of 10 percent ad valorem on goods of economies that: impose a forced labor import prohibition but do not yet effectively enforce it (Canada, Ecuador, the European Union, Indonesia, Mexico, and Pakistan); have undertaken commitments ... (Argentina, Bangladesh, Cambodia, Ecuador, El Salvador, Guatemala, Indonesia, Malaysia, and Taiwan); or have imposed a partial regime ... (the United Kingdom)." Accurate.
- Memo recital line 149-152 "proposed ... zero section 301 tariff rate" vs proposal "reduced" — good.
- Memo recital line 156-159 "USTR received over 1,600 written comments and testimony from over 100 witnesses" vs June proposal's 450/nearly 60 for initiation—those are different, but the memo says "on these proposed actions," which is correct.
- Notice at 47318 line 158-161 says "reduced Section 301 tariff rate" correct.
- Notice at 47318 line 168-169 "proposed applying tariffs of 12.5 percent for every other economy" correct.
- Notice at 47318 line 170-174 "all articles and parts ... subject to Section 232" correct for proposal.
- Notice at 47319 line 218-222 "over 1,600 comments / over 100 witnesses" correct.
- Notice at 47330 line 1539 says "exempt all products proposed for exemption in Annex A, except non-pharmaceutical applications of certain chemical products." June proposal proposed exemptions for chemical products? likely yes.
- Notice at 47331 line 1648 "additional 471 products" maybe memo Annex differs; image.
- Notice at 47334 line 2030-2032 says auto parts subject to 232 exempt; operative note 52(f)(3) limited list. Could list as discrepancy if strong.
- Notice at 47352 note 52(a) says headings 9903.05.20-9903.05.84 impose duties "on imports of all products of the countries provided for in these headings"; but note 52(f) exempts many products. "Except as provided..." so fine.
- Notice at 47394 Annex II note says "All products that are properly classified in the provisions ... listed in this Annex are not covered by the actions, except as provided in the 'Scope Limitations' column." But note 52(f)-(k) exemptions are not in Annex II. Fine.

Another potential discrepancy: The memo Section 1(a)(ii) says "For a product of Japan, Korea, or Switzerland..." and notice specific determination for South Korea also net. Fine.
But the memo Section 1(a)(ii) heading says "Tariff rate of 10 percent or 12.5 percent, net of MFN rate," while the text says for Japan/Korea/Switzerland sum 12.5; okay.

Maybe a discrepancy in the notice's specific determination for Japan: it says "except as provided in Annex I and Annex II, Part A" (no Part for Japan-specific exemptions), but memo Section 1(b)(v) does not list Japan among economies with negotiated exemptions. Consistent.
For Korea: same.
For EU: Part C; memo lists EU. Consistent.
For Taiwan: Part K; memo lists Taiwan. Consistent.

Maybe the June proposal says "For economies that impose a forced labor import prohibition ... the Trade Representative proposes additional duties of 10% for products of these economies." It lists Canada, Ecuador, EU, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan. But the final notice's determinations say six economies "failed to effectively enforce" including those. Consistent.

Let's search for "zero" in memo and notice.

content.text:
Excellent: clear discrepancy: memo says proposal was "zero section 301 tariff rate" (91 FR 47719); June proposal says "reduced Section 301 tariff rate" (91 FR 34274); notice correctly says reduced (47318). This is a Q11 item.

Any other memo descriptions of proposal:
- Memo line 134-144: "proposed tariffs of 10 percent ... on goods of economies that impose a forced labor import prohibition but do not yet effectively enforce it (Canada, Ecuador, EU, Indonesia, Mexico, Pakistan)" — June proposal yes.
- Memo line 149-152 zero vs reduced — discrepancy.
- Memo line 167-176: "certain products warrant exemption ... including because of needs..." accurate.
- Memo line 195-203: "The Trade Representative has also advised me that for goods of the European Union, Japan, Korea, Switzerland, or Taiwan, section 301 tariffs that are the net of MFN tariffs would be consistent..." This is advice, not proposal; June proposal had no net-of-MFN. Fine.
- Memo line 225-239: additional economies at 10%; okay.

Maybe another section 301 discrepancy: The notice at 47318 says "The June 5, 2026 FRN proposed applying tariffs of 10 percent for each economy that imposes a forced labor import prohibition" but the June proposal's 10% group includes economies with ART commitments and a partial regime; it's not only economies that impose. The sentence structure includes "has taken on commitments ... or has imposed a partial regime"; so okay.

Maybe the notice at 47318 says "The June 5, 2026 FRN proposed applying tariffs of 12.5 percent for every other economy." But the June proposal's 12.5% group includes countries that later moved; okay.

Maybe the memo's statement "USTR received over 1,600 written comments and testimony from over 100 witnesses at the hearings" is accurate.

Maybe the notice's statement "The Trade Representative has determined ... 10 percent ... with specific economies subject to a 10 percent rate net of a product's MFN duty" but in fact only EU and Taiwan are 10% net; "specific economies" is vague.

Let's search for "all products" vs "all goods" in memo and notice; no.

Maybe another discrepancy: Notice at 47319 says "The Trade Representative also informed the President of economies that have imposed forced labor import prohibitions, or undertaken commitments ... since June 5, 2026." It lists in next paragraph 6 bans + Jordan. Fine.
Memo says "additional economies have imposed ... (Cambodia, Guatemala, Honduras, India, Sri Lanka, and Trinidad and Tobago) or undertaken commitments ... (Jordan)." Fine.

Maybe the memo's Sec. 1(b)(v) negotiated exemptions list includes "Ecuador" but the June proposal listed Ecuador among both 10% groups; okay.

Maybe Q11 can include a section 301 discrepancy between the notice's FTZ statement and the memo? Memo has no FTZ. No.

Maybe Q11 expects the discrepancy between the notice's claim that "the tariff proposals ... included exemptions for ... all articles and parts of articles subject to tariffs under Section 232" and the adopted text's narrower section 232 exemption; but that's a change, and Q11 explicitly says "A change between the June proposal and the adopted text is not in itself a discrepancy; it is one only where a document describes the proposal or the adopted text inaccurately." The notice's description of the proposal is accurate. However, the notice at 47334 says "many inputs, including auto parts already subject to Section 232 tariffs, are exempt from additional tariffs pursuant to this action." If the adopted text only exempts listed headings, this statement describes the adopted text overbroadly. That's a discrepancy between preamble and operative text. Could list.

Similarly, notice at 47318 says "exemptions as provided in Annexes I and II" but operative note 52(a)-(k) adds exemptions; that's a preamble statement about adopted text that is incomplete. Is incomplete a discrepancy? It says "certain exemptions as provided in Annexes I and II"; maybe "certain" not exhaustive. Hmm.

And notice at 2048 "maximum tariffs of 12.5 percent" vs operative rates (12.5% plus MFN) could be another overstatement. But "tariffs" likely section 301 only.

Let's read the memo/notice Section 1(b) phrase "products identified in the Annex to this memorandum" vs notice's Annexes I and II. The memo says exemptions in "the Annex"; notice says Annexes I and II. Could be the same content split. Not discrepancy.

Maybe Q11 expected list is around 4-6 items; we can provide the strong ones and note that no other contradictions were found. The answer can include:
1. Aug 19 vs Aug 22 recitals (all six later proclamations).
2. 11056 amendment only chapeau, leaving operative clauses at Aug 19.
3. 11062 cross-reference to nonexistent dairy scope proclamation.
4. 11064/11065/11076 recital 30-day waiting period vs 7-day operative effective dates for newly added products.
5. Memo says June proposal's textile mechanism was at a zero section 301 rate; June proposal and notice say reduced rate.
6. Notice's response-to-comments statement that auto parts subject to section 232 are exempt vs operative note 52(f)(3)'s enumerated headings (and Q9(e) confirms non-mentioned section 232 headings are not exempt).
7. Notice summary says exemptions are "as provided in Annexes I and II," while operative note 52(a)-(k) creates additional exemptions outside the Annexes (chapter 98, civil aircraft, pharma, section 232, USMCA, CAFTA, accompanied baggage). Is this a discrepancy? Could list as "description vs operative text" but risk over-listing. Q11 says "list as many as you can find"; over-inclusion with explanation may be okay if genuine. But "Do not list matters on which a document is merely silent." This is not silence; it's an incomplete description. Hmm.
8. Notice says "The Trade Representative is taking actions ... by imposing tariffs on all products of the investigated economy, with certain exemptions as provided in Annexes I and II" — also note 52(g)/(h) exempts USMCA Canada/Mexico, not in Annexes. Could be same as 7.
9. June proposal says "proposed action does not cover ... all articles and parts of articles that are subject to section 232 tariffs"; notice's response says "many inputs, including auto parts ... are exempt"; okay.

Maybe also: 11062 clause (3) says "this proclamation does not otherwise affect the products, as further established in the Proclamation of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope ... With Respect to Dairy)"—not only nonexistent but the phrase "as further established" implies dairy scope was modified, which it wasn't. Strong.

Could list 11062's title says "Dairy" but clause (1) says "certain products of Canada" without limiting to dairy—annex presumably dairy. Not necessary.

Now Q1 "what it does" one line each. Need mention 11056's refund clause maybe.

Now let's double-check Q5(b) filing date of October proclamation: "Filed 10-29-26; 11:15 am" at 91 FR 68871. Signed Oct 23. Published Oct 30. Good.

Q5(b) September scope signed Sept 8, filed Sept 11, published Sept 14. Not asked but can mention.

Q5(c) "As these documents describe section 338, there is a waiting period before additional duties may take effect. How long after signing did P and S become dutiable" — P: 7 days (Sept 8→Sept 15); S: 7 days (Oct 23→Oct 30). Recital 8/9 says not earlier than 30 days after "the President's proclamation finding." The scope proclamations do not explain. Also note original findings July 20; by Sept 15, 57 days had passed; by Oct 30, 102 days. Could mention that one possible reading is the 30-day clock runs from the original July 20 finding, but the documents do not say that. This is important: For P and S, the "proclamation finding" might be the original Proclamation 11048's finding on July 20, so 30 days had long passed; the scope proclamations don't need a new finding? But they do not explain. We'll flag.

Q3(c) court ruling: "What applies to shipments of it imported after that ruling, and under which provision?" Answer: 50% ad valorem duty under 11061 clause (9)(b), because invalidated import ban triggers the 50% duty in 11046 for imports to which ban had applied. Cite 91 FR 58313. If the ruling is "as applied to this beer" and the beer is in the Annex, clause (9)(b) applies. Good.

Q3(d): No; clause (3) says proclamation doesn't otherwise affect products subject to 11046 as established by the scope modification. The 50% duty remains for non-Annex listed products. Cite 91 FR 58313.

Q2(c): What do documents say about getting it back? Proclamation 11056 clause (4) says refunds processed pursuant to applicable law and CBP standard procedures. Clause (2) directs suspension of collection. No further detail. Cite 91 FR 54790-91.

Now Q10 Scenario 2(e): "A shipment that arrives on October 2, 2026." The exclusion proclamation 11061 applies to goods "imported on or after Sept 29." So excluded. But is whisky an "alcoholic beverage" in Annex? Yes. So prohibited. However, clause (2) says products subject to ban that were imported but not yet entered before Sept 29 remain subject to 50% duty. This shipment arrives Oct 2, so not imported before Sept 29; banned. Answer: no duty; inadmissible. Section 301? If it cannot be imported, no. We can say the 50% section 338 duty is replaced by the import ban; the 10% section 301 does not apply because entry is prohibited (and if it were somehow entered, Canada's 10% would apply; but no lawful entry). Better to say "It may not be imported; no duty is assessed because the goods are excluded. If CBP were to permit entry, the section 301 Canada rate of 10% would be the only additional duty, because section 338 duty is replaced by the ban"—but the question asks section 338 + section 301 + total. We'll say section 338: not applicable (import prohibited); section 301: no entry; total: none. Flag that the documents do not expressly address duty on unlawfully imported goods.

Q10 Scenario 1(a): Section 301 Canada 10% but exempt under note 52(f)(1) because aluminum article under 9903.82.02. Need cite note 52(f)(1): 91 FR 47362-47363. Yes, line 2461 at page 47362. Good.
Scenario 1(b): Section 338 applies via 11065 clause (1) (motor vehicles scope modification) because the extrusions are in Annex II and not on Part B; effective Sept 15. Cite 91 FR 58340. But wait: Does the section 338 motor-vehicles duty apply to aluminum extrusions? Scenario says listed in Annex II since signed; yes. The scope modification was for motor vehicles but includes extrusions. Fine.
Scenario 2(c): Section 338 50% on whisky; but is whisky subject to section 232? no. So duty applies from Aug 22. USMCA no exemption. Good.
Scenario 2(d): Section 301 Canada 10%. Is whisky exempt under any note 52 list? No (alcoholic beverages not exempt). Good.
Scenario 2(e): import ban.

Q10(f): Neither. Cite EO 14389 and Proc. 11012.

Now Q2(d): "Did the duties need a further presidential action in order to begin?" Could also refer to the fact that Proclamation 11056's suspension was set to last 3 days, but the original proclamations said duties effective Aug 19; if no further action, they would begin Aug 22 automatically. Later documents say that's what happened. Yes.

Now Q1 "Say which kind of event that date and time is measured against in each document." For original duty proclamations and scope modifications: "goods entered for consumption, or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption, on or after" the time. For suspension: same (effective date of duties). For exclusion proclamations: "goods imported on or after" the time. For 11056: it changes effective date for entries/withdrawals. Good.

Now Q1 "for each of the three product groups, which documents changed which products are subject to the duty." We can phrase:
- Alcoholic beverages: 11046 imposed on Annex II. 11064 (Annex I Part A added; Part B removed; effective Sept 15). 11061 (Annex products excluded from importation effective Sept 29; no longer "subject to duty" but banned). No other.
- Dairy: 11047 imposed on Annex II. 11062 (Annex products excluded from importation effective Sept 29). No scope modification; 11062's reference to one is erroneous.
- Motor vehicles: 11048 imposed on Annex II. 11065 (Part A added; Part B removed; Sept 15). 11076 (Part A removed; Part B added; Oct 30). 11063 (Annex products excluded from importation effective Sept 29). Note 11063's import ban may overlap with products subject to duty; once banned, no duty on imports after Sept 29.
Also 11064/11065/11076 state duties apply in addition to section 232, changing the section 232 carve-out.

Now Q4 exact quote/cite:
- For Sept 10: original clause (2): "The duties imposed in this proclamation shall not apply to articles subject to duties pursuant to section 232..." 91 FR 46641 (alcohol), 46655 (dairy), 46665 (motor vehicles). So all three section 338 = 0; section 232 25% = $25,000 each.
- For Oct 1: X: 11064 clause (1): "The duties imposed pursuant to Proclamation 11046, as modified in this proclamation, shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232..." effective Sept 15. 91 FR 58332. So 232 $25,000 + 338 $50,000 = $75,000.
Y: no scope modification; original clause (2) still excludes section 232 → 232 $25,000 + 338 $0 = $25,000.
Z: 11065 clause (1) same language; 91 FR 58340. 232 $25,000 + 338 $50,000 = $75,000.
But wait Q4 asks "give the section 232 duty and the section 338 duty on X, Y and Z" not total. So list separately.

Now Q4(c) exact text:
- Quote original clause (2) for each.
- Quote 11064/11065 clause (1) "shall apply in addition to duties imposed pursuant to section 232".
- Cite pages.
- For Y, cite absence of dairy scope modification and 11062 clause (3) erroneous reference maybe.

Now Q5(a) table:
Time | P | Q | R | S
Sept 14 3pm: P no; Q yes; R yes; S no.
Sept 15 12:01am: P yes; Q no; R yes; S no.
Oct 29 4pm: P yes; Q no; R yes; S no.
Oct 30 12:01am: P yes; Q no; R no; S yes.
Nov 3: P yes; Q no; R no; S yes.
Explain: P Part A Sept = newly subject Sept 15, not removed Oct; Q Part B Sept = removed Sept 15, not re-added Oct; R Part A Oct = removed Oct 30; S Part B Oct = added Oct 30.
Note "duty applies" means 50% section 338 on entry/withdrawal.

Q5(b): October signed Oct 23; filed Oct 29; published Oct 30; applies Oct 30 12:01 a.m. ET. Scope proclamations do not reach entries before effective date; operate only on entry/withdrawal on/after. No refunds. Cite 11076 clause (1)-(2) 91 FR 68862; 11065 clause (1)-(2) 91 FR 58340. Also no refund provision in 11064/11065/11076; contrast 11056 clause (4) refund provision.
Q5(c): 7 days; recitals 8/9 at 58340/68862 state 30-day limit; no explanation. Could mention original finding July 20.

Now Q6(c) details:
- Switzerland: proposed 12.5% flat (June proposal lines 319-330; Switzerland not in 10% list); adopted 12.5% net (notice 47327), so effective 301 lower where MFN >0.
- Germany/EU: proposed 10% flat; adopted 10% net (notice 47323).
- Taiwan: proposed 10% flat; adopted 10% net (notice 47327).
- Japan: proposed 12.5% flat; adopted 12.5% net (notice 47324).
- India: proposed 12.5%; adopted 10%; reason India adopted forced labor import prohibition after June 5 (notice 47324; memo 47720).
- Norway, UK, Türkiye, Hong Kong, Liechtenstein: unchanged/not investigated. UK proposed 10% and adopted 10% (no net); Norway/Türkiye/Hong Kong 12.5% both; Liechtenstein not in 60.
Need maybe note Switzerland was in June 10%? No, Switzerland is not in 10% list; 12.5.
Also note "adopted treatment differ" for Japan due net; EU/Taiwan due net; Switzerland due net.

Q7(a) arithmetic:
3 cents/kg × 2,000 kg = $60.
$60 / $12,000 = 0.005 = 0.5% ad valorem equivalent.
EU cap 10%; section 301 rate = 10% - 0.5% = 9.5%.
9.5% × $12,000 = $1,140.
Q7(b):
Specific: 25 cents × 4,000 = $1,000.
Ad valorem: 4% × $20,000 = $800.
Total column 1 = $1,800; equivalent = 9%.
Italy EU cap 10% → 1% × 20,000 = $200.
Japan cap 12.5% → 3.5% × 20,000 = $700.
Brazil flat 12.5% → $2,500 (no net; note 52(k) doesn't apply to Brazil).
Q7(c):
$2,200 / $20,000 = 11%.
Taiwan cap 10% → MFN ≥10, 301 = 0.
Switzerland cap 12.5% → MFN <12.5, 301 = 1.5% × 20,000 = $300. Wait! I earlier said 0 for Switzerland. Let's recalc: 11% < 12.5%, so 301 = 12.5% - 11% = 1.5% × $20,000 = $300. Yes! I mistakenly said 0. Correct: Taiwan 0; Switzerland $300. Good catch.
Q6(b) Japan MFN 12% → 0.5% = $500 correct.
Q7(c) Taiwan 11% ≥10 → 0; Switzerland 11% <12.5 → 1.5% = $300.

Q7(d): Rule at U.S. note 52(k) 91 FR 47392; result: for headings 9903.05.39/9903.05.76 (EU/Taiwan 10% cap), articles with column 1 duty rate less than 10% sum to 10%; if equivalent ≥10%, additional zero. For headings 9903.05.49/.71/.74 (Japan/Korea/Switzerland 12.5% cap), less than 12.5% sum to 12.5%; if ≥12.5%, zero. The specific determinations state zero at or above cap (e.g., 47323, 47324, 47327). Good.

Q8 details:
1. Loaded July 22, entered July 29 → $10,000.
2. Entered July 27 3pm → 0.
3. Entered July 28 12:01am → $10,000.
4. Loaded July 24 6am → $10,000.
5. Entered July 23 → 0.
6. Warehouse withdrawal July 26 → $10,000.
7. Air July 23, entered July 25 → $10,000.
Explain each against DATES: duties apply to entries on/after July 24 12:01 a.m.; transit exception only for goods loaded onto a vessel before July 24 12:01 and entered before July 28 12:01. Door 1 loaded July 22 before deadline, but entered July 29 after July 28 deadline → duty. Door 2 both conditions met → exempt. Door 3 entered exactly 12:01 July 28, not "before" → duty. Door 4 loaded after deadline → no exception. Door 5 entered before July 24 → duty not yet applicable. Door 6 no vessel transit; withdrawal after July 24 → duty. Door 7 aircraft not vessel → no exception.

Q1.answer: Ten section 338 documents: (1) Proc. 11046, Doc. 2026-14991, 91 FR 46639, signed 7/20/26, published 7/23/26—50% duty on Annex II Canadian alcoholic beverages; operative from 12:01 a.m. ET 8/22/26 as amended (originally printed 8/19), measured against goods entered for consumption or withdrawn from warehouse for consumption. (2) Proc. 11047, 2026-14992, 91 FR 46653, signed 7/20, published 7/23—same 50% duty on Annex II dairy; same date/event. (3) Proc. 11048, 2026-14997, 91 FR 46663, signed 7/20, published 7/23—same 50% duty on Annex II motor vehicles; same date/event. (4) Proc. 11056, 2026-17294, 91 FR 54789, signed 8/18, published 8/24—3-day suspension; changes effective date to 12:01 a.m. ET 8/22/26, measured against entry/withdrawal; amends Annex II chapeaux and provides refunds. (5) Proc. 11061, 2026-18835, 91 FR 58311, signed 9/8, published 9/14—excludes certain alcoholic beverages from importation from 12:01 a.m. ET 9/29/26, measured against goods imported (physical importation). (6) Proc. 11062, 2026-18836, 91 FR 58319, signed 9/8, published 9/14—same import exclusion for dairy. (7) Proc. 11063, 2026-18837, 91 FR 58325, signed 9/8, published 9/14—same import exclusion for motor vehicles. (8) Proc. 11064, 2026-18838, 91 FR 58331, signed 9/8, published 9/14—alcoholic scope modification: Annex I-A adds, Annex I-B removes; duties apply in addition to §232; from 12:01 a.m. ET 9/15/26, entry/withdrawal. (9) Proc. 11065, 2026-18839, 91 FR 58339, signed 9/8, published 9/14—motor-vehicle scope modification: Annex I-A adds, Annex I-B removes; duties apply in addition to §232; from 12:01 a.m. ET 9/15/26, entry/withdrawal. (10) Proc. 11076, 2026-22292, 91 FR 68861, signed 10/23, filed 10/29, published 10/30—further motor-vehicle scope modification: Annex I-A removes, Annex I-B adds; duties apply in addition to §232; from 12:01 a.m. ET 10/30/26, entry/withdrawal. Product groups: alcoholic—11046 imposed; 11064 changed scope; 11061 converted listed products to an import ban. Dairy—11047 imposed; 11062 converted listed products to a ban; no dairy scope modification was published (11062's reference to one is erroneous). Motor vehicles—11048 imposed; 11065 and 11076 changed scope; 11063 converted listed products to a ban.

Q11.answer: Discrepancies found: (1) In each of 11061, 11062, 11063, 11064, 11065 and 11076, recital 1 says the §338 duties were "effective August 19, 2026," while recital 4 of the same document says they "became effective" at 12:01 a.m. on August 22, 2026 (91 FR 58311, 58319, 58325, 58331, 58339, 68861). (2) 11056 clause (1) states that the effective date "shall be" August 22 and that "accordingly" only "the chapeau of Annex II" is amended, but the operative clauses (1) and (3) of 11046/47/48 still print August 19 (54790 vs. 46641, 46655, 46665). (3) 11062 clause (3) refers to a "Proclamation of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope ... With Respect to Dairy)" that was never issued; no dairy scope modification appears in the Federal Register (58320). (4) 11064/11065/11076 recitals state the §338 30-day waiting period, but their operative clauses make newly listed products dutiable 7 days after signing (58332, 58340, 68862). (5) The §301 memorandum says the June proposal's textile mechanism would allow imports "at a zero section 301 tariff rate" (47719), while the June proposal and the notice say "a reduced Section 301 tariff rate" (34274; 47318). (2) Proc. 11047, 2026-14992, 91 FR 46653, signed 7/20, published 7/23—same 50% duty on Annex II dairy; same date/event. (4) Proc. 11056, 2026-17294, 91 FR 54789, signed 8/18, published 8/24—3-day suspension; changes effective date to 12:01 a.m. ET 8/22/26, measured against entry/withdrawal; amends Annex II chapeaux and provides refunds. Q2.answer: (a) Entry 1 (8/20, 2 p.m.): $0. Entry 2 (8/21, 11:59 p.m.): $0. Entry 3 (8/22, 12:01 a.m.): $40,000 × 50% = $20,000. (b) 11046 clauses (1) and (3) print August 19, 2026. Proc. 11056 clause (1) says the effective date of the duties in 11046/47/48 "shall be 12:01 a.m. ... August 22, 2026," and amends only "the chapeau of Annex II" of each proclamation, replacing August 19 with August 22. The operative clauses (1)/(3) were not amended and still print August 19. The later-in-time operative clause (1), plus 11056 clause (5) (inconsistent prior provisions superseded), resolves it in favor of August 22; later proclamations recite that the duties became effective August 22. (c) Proc. 11056 clause (4): refunds "shall be processed pursuant to applicable law and CBP's standard procedures for such refunds"; clause (2) also directed suspension of collection. (d) No further presidential action was needed. Later documents state Canada reneged on August 21, 2026, and that at 12:01 a.m. ET on August 22 the 3-day suspension lapsed and the duties became effective. (e) Section 338 permits duties not to take effect earlier than 30 days after the President's proclamation finding. Signed July 20: July 20-31 = 11 days; August 1-19 = 19 days; 11 + 19 = 30, so August 19 was the earliest permissible date.
Q2.uncertainty: The original clauses (1)/(3) were never formally amended and still print August 19; the documents do not explain this drafting gap.

Q11.answer: Discrepancies found: (1) In each of 11061, 11062, 11063, 11064, 11065 and 11076, recital 1 says the §338 duties were "effective August 19, 2026," while recital 4 of the same document says they "became effective" at 12:01 a.m. on August 22, 2026 (91 FR 58311, 58319, 58325, 58331, 58339, 68861). (2) 11056 clause (1) states that the effective date "shall be" August 22 and that "accordingly" only "the chapeau of Annex II" is amended, but the operative clauses (1) and (3) of 11046/47/48 still print August 19 (54790 vs. 46641, 46655, 46665). (3) 11062 clause (3) refers to a "Proclamation of September 8, 2026 (Modifying the Scope ... With Respect to Dairy)" that was never issued; no dairy scope modification appears in the Federal Register (58320). (4) 11064/11065/11076 recitals state the §338 30-day waiting period, but their operative clauses make newly listed products dutiable 7 days after signing (58332, 58340, 68862). (5) The §301 memorandum says the June proposal's textile mechanism would allow imports "at a zero section 301 tariff rate" (47719), while the June proposal and the notice say "a reduced Section 301 tariff rate" (34274; 47318). (6) The notice's response-to-comments statement that "many inputs, including auto parts already subject to Section 232 tariffs, are exempt" (47334) is accurate only for the headings enumerated in note 52(f)(3) (47362-63); a §232 heading not listed is not exempt (see Q9(e)).
Q11.uncertainty: Whether item (6) is a true discrepancy or merely imprecise shorthand is arguable; the first five are textual conflicts.
